entries.reason: CodeQL counts a call of verify... or ...Authentication... as authorization, so it flags the three passkey routes of server/src/auth.ts (register/verify, sign-in/options, sign-in/verify), and the server has no rate limiter the query knows (express-rate-limit and the like). One owner, one-time challenges, recovery codes of 100 bits: nothing there can be guessed, but it can be repeated: 100 unauthenticated POST /api/auth/sign-in/options evict the owner's waiting sign-in (maxCeremonies, oldest first), so sign-in can be blocked while a flood lasts; that exposure was there before this entry. The app shell route (res.sendFile) is not expected to be flagged any more, because it sends the index.html read at start; the entry is limited to server/src/auth.ts, so a result of this rule in any other file fails the codeql job. Issue #45 adds a limiter the query recognises and removes this entry.

Not a secret: the test fixture "dG9rZW4=.c2lnbg==" in server/src/auth.test.ts is the base64 of the words "token" and "sign", a made-up session cookie value with base64 padding for the test that a cookie value containing = is read whole. It opens no session and grants nothing. Commit a5985c0 stays in the history, so the finding is excused by its fingerprint until the entry runs out; #35 tracks the security gates and removes the entry.
